itinerary.notes: Fly Reykjavík to Gdańsk (~3h30, booked). Drop bags, then Długi Targ, the Gdańsk Crane and the Motława at dusk, Mariacka Street, pierogi at Mandu, beers on Piwna.
Museum of the Second World War at opening, then the European Solidarity Centre at the shipyard. Both shut Mondays, so this is the only clean slot. Evening at Pub Spółdzielczy.
Morning PKP IC to Kraków (~5h30). Afternoon in Kazimierz on foot, zapiekanka at Endziora on Plac Nowy, night at Alchemia.
Auschwitz-Birkenau on an official guided slot: a full day, ~1h30 each way. Keep the evening light; Florianska cellar bars if anyone still wants one.
Wieliczka Salt Mine in the morning (3.5 km route, ~2-3h underground), Rynek Underground and Wawel in the afternoon, kiełbasa from the blue van, then the 20:57 night train to Munich.

Arrive München Hbf 10:39. Bags down, then Marienplatz and the Glockenspiel, lunch at the Viktualienmarkt, the Englischer Garten and the Eisbach surfers, first beer garden of the trip. Group grows to ~10.
Morning at the Asamkirche and the Residenz. OKTOBERFEST (booked): tents open 10:00, last beer 22:30, close midnight. Friday before a public holiday, so the busiest evening of the run.
German Unity Day: shops shut, museums and beer gardens open. Dachau Memorial in the morning (free, S-Bahn plus bus), Augustiner Bräustuben or the Hirschgarten afterwards.
Viktualienmarkt is closed on Sundays, so make it Nymphenburg or Olympiapark instead, then the ICE to Cologne (~4h30). Exchange block 1 starts on arrival.
Exchange programme owns the day; evening commitments. Free-window pick: Kölner Dom interior, then the Hohenzollern Bridge love-locks walk to Deutz at dusk.
Programme. Free-window pick: NS-Dokumentationszentrum in the EL-DE Haus, the preserved Gestapo house-prison.
Programme. Evening: a proper brauhaus crawl, Päffgen then Früh em Veedel, 0.2L at a time until you cap the glass with the coaster.
Programme. Evening: Zülpicher Straße and the Kwartier Latäng student strip, MTC cellar club if there is energy left.
Programme. Evening: Club Bahnhof Ehrenfeld under the railway arches, or live jazz at Stadtgarten.
If the programme leaves the day free: Aachen (35-60 min, Eurail), Charlemagne's cathedral and coronation throne. Otherwise Ehrenfeld street art and Belgisches Viertel.
Slow day. Rheinauhafen and the Kranhäuser on foot, the KölnTriangle deck for the cathedral-and-bridges frame, then Lommerzheim in Deutz for the pork chop (cash only).
Programme. Free-window pick: Römerturm and the Praetorium, then dinner in the Severinsviertel.
Train Cologne to Luxembourg (~3h30-4h). Chemin de la Corniche at golden hour, dinner in the Grund, then Rives de Clausen. Domestic transport is free, so use the trams and lifts freely.
Bock Casemates and the free Pfaffenthal panoramic lift in the morning, then the train to Ghent via Brussels (~3h30). Graslei at dusk, Kwak at Dulle Griet.
The Ghent Altarpiece at St Bavo's on a timed slot, Gravensteen, Patershol, Werregarenstraat graffiti alley. Film Fest Gent is running (7-18 Oct), so book food. Overpoort student bars at night.
Vrijdagmarkt in the morning, then Bruges (~30 min) for the afternoon and evening: go late and you get the canals without the coach crowds.

IC train Ghent to Amsterdam via Antwerp and Rotterdam (~3h30). Do not take the Eurostar high-speed, it needs a paid reservation. Afternoon: Albert Cuypmarkt and Noordermarkt (Saturday), apple pie at Winkel 43, De Pijp bars.
Canal Ring on foot (Brouwersgracht, the 9 Streets), Anne Frank House on a pre-booked timed ticket, then the free IJ ferry to Noord for EYE and NDSM. Markets are shut on Sundays.
Utrecht for the day (~30 min, Eurail): the canal wharf cellars, the Dom Tower, a livelier and less touristed centre than Haarlem.
SLOW DAY, deliberately placed mid-stay. One museum only (Rijksmuseum or Van Gogh, booked ahead), then the Jordaan brown cafés and Vondelpark.
Haarlem for the half-day (~15-20 min), back for the ADE opening: Jean-Michel Jarre at AFAS Live, 20:00, tickets from EUR 76.29, or a Resident Advisor club night instead.

Fly Amsterdam to Madrid via Palma on two separate tickets. Self-transfer: reclaim and re-check six bags. Only leave PMI on a 5h gap, store bags at the Plaça d'Espanya lockers, and be back at check-in T-minus 90 minutes. Group becomes 6.
Museo Sorolla in the morning, then La Latina: Mercado de la Cebada and the 9th-century Muralla Árabe. Cerro del Tío Pío for sunset, Malasaña and Calle Argumosa at night.
El Capricho park and the Jaca Civil War bunker, open weekends and holidays only so it has to be today. Afternoon free, then collect the seven-seat minivan in the evening.

Clocks go back 03:00 to 02:00. Drive to Córdoba (~3h50), lunch at Taberna Salinas, Mezquita on the 15:00 slot (no Sunday morning free window, and it shuts 11:30-15:00 for Mass), then on to Sevilla (~1h30).

Skydive Spain, early slot. Afternoon deliberately slow. Casa Morales and the Alameda de Hércules in the evening, Casa Anselma in Triana for spontaneous flamenco (shut Sundays, so tonight or tomorrow).

Backup jump window. If the jump is done: Real Alcázar (shut Mondays, open today), Triana and the free Inquisition ruins under the market at the Castillo de San Jorge, Mercado de Feria, tablao at night.

Drive Sevilla to Ronda (~1h45) with a short stop at Osuna. Puente Nuevo and the gorge path, the 13th-century Baños Árabes, then a quiet tapas round on Plaza del Socorro. Midweek small town, so no club night.
Ronda to Setenil for lunch under the rock, then Granada (~3h total). El Torcal only if you are away by 09:30. Evening: big free tapas at Bodegas Castañeda, then Calle Elvira.
Alhambra with the booked Nasrid Palaces morning slot. Afternoon: Realejo murals and the Carmen de los Mártires gardens. Hammam Al Ándalus in the evening (book days ahead), then Granada 10.

Granada to València (~4h50) via the Guadix cave quarter. Mercat Central shuts around 15:00 and is closed tomorrow, so only if you get in early. Halloween in Ruzafa: dinner 21:00, bars 23:00, clubs 00:30 to 06:00, costume expected.

All Saints. Drive to Barcelona (~4h) with a coffee stop at Peñíscola. Return the minivan on arrival at El Prat, or a Sants slot confirmed in writing. Razzmatazz runs on holiday eves, so tonight works.

Transferred holiday: markets and most shops shut. Búnkers del Carmel for the free 360, Refugi 307 air-raid shelter, Gràcia squares, EUR 1-2 pintxos on Carrer Blai. Nasty Mondays at Sala Apolo, EUR 15 with a drink.
La Boqueria and the Sagrada Família in the morning, both open on a Tuesday after two holiday days. Afternoon flight to Venice (~1h55). Back to the core four.
Rialto Market before it winds down at noon, cicchetti at the Erbaria. Cannaregio and the 1516 Jewish Ghetto in the afternoon. Bacaro crawl on Fondamenta della Misericordia in the evening.
Verona for the day (~1h10 on a fast train): the Roman Arena, Piazza delle Erbe, Castelvecchio. No opera in November, that season is summer only.

Unstructured day. San Marco at opening, Libreria Acqua Alta, then Dorsoduro and the Zattere out to Punta della Dogana at dusk. Campo Santa Margherita at night. Burano and Torcello instead if it is clear.
Day train Venice to Vienna over the UNESCO Semmering line (~7h15). Passholder reservation is compulsory on the Italian cross-border leg. Evening: Stephansplatz Christmas market, open from 6 Nov.

THE HIKE. Wachau Welterbesteig Stage 1, Krems to Dürnstein: 12.5 km, ~4h30, 350-490 m of climb, yellow waymarks. Train to reach Krems by 09:00, Postbus 715 back. Sunset 16:27, so be in Dürnstein by 14:30.
Zentralfriedhof by tram 71 for Beethoven, Schubert and Strauss. Naschmarkt (shut Sundays, open today), Café Sperl, Schönbrunn and its market. Wien Modern or the Donaukanal bars at night.

Train to Bratislava (~1h), bags into the station lockers, 3-4 hours in the Old Town plus bryndzové halušky at Nová Tržnica, then the EC on to Budapest (~2h30). Skip Slavín, it is too far uphill for a day stop.
Rudas: the 16th-century Turkish bath plus the rooftop tub over the Danube, men-only on Wednesdays, ~12,000 HUF. Hospital in the Rock (guided only, book ahead), then the House of Terror.

Memento Park and its communist statues, lángos at the Great Market Hall, Fisherman's Bastion at dusk. Veli Bej or Lukács for the quieter local bath. Madách tér for a night where Hungarians actually drink.
EC Budapest to Prague (~7h). Evening in Žižkov: U Vystřeleného oka, then tank Pilsner at Lokál. The Friday bath party at Rudas or Széchenyi is not reachable on a travel day, so let it go.

Prague Castle and St Vitus at opening, down through Malá Strana, Charles Bridge, Letná Beer Garden for the panorama. This is also the reserve slot for the Pravčická brána hike if the Wachau got washed out.
Kutná Hora (~1h by train): the Sedlec Ossuary and St Barbara's. Terezín is the WWII alternative if the group would rather have the ghetto memorial than the bone church.

Vyšehrad, where the 1989 student march began, then the Náplavka embankment cellars and Nový Svět lane. Original Beer Spa in the evening (two tubs for four, ~CZK 6,600 with sauna). U Zlatého tygra right after opening.

Velvet Revolution day. Candles at the raised-hands memorial at Národní 16 and the Korzo Národní festival in the morning, then the ~7h30 train to Cologne, changing at Frankfurt, Mannheim or Dresden. The 17:11 singing of Modlitba pro Martu is the trade-off you are making.
Exam block begins. The Cathedral, Neumarkt and Rudolfplatz Christmas markets have been open since 16 Nov. Glühwein under the Dom in the evening.
Study or exams. Free window: NS-Dokumentationszentrum if block 1 missed it, then Ehrenfeld for the evening.
Study or exams. Harbour market at the Schokoladenmuseum, then Zülpicher Straße.
FOOTBALL BACKUP: Schalke 04 vs VfB Stuttgart at the Veltins-Arena, ~1h by train, kickoff likely 15:30, standing EUR 18-25 and seats EUR 35-55. If the match is skipped, Aachen or Bonn instead.

Totensonntag: the Cathedral and Heinzels markets are closed for the day, which makes this the right day to leave the city. Drachenfels and the Siebengebirge from Königswinter (45 min, 3-5h, Rhine views and two castle ruins).
Exams. Heinzels Wintermärchen opens today on the Alter Markt and Heumarkt, ice rink included.
Exams. Evening at Lommerzheim in Deutz for the pork chop and Päffgen Kölsch, if block 1 did not get there.
Last full day in Cologne. All six markets open at once, Severinsviertel and Belgisches Viertel, then pack for a long travel day.
ICE plus EC via Hamburg (~9h30-10h, one change). A full travel day, no reservation obligation in late November. Late arrival, one beer in Nørrebro, nothing else.
LIGHT DAY by design. Smørrebrød at Torvehallerne, Nyhavn and Indre By on foot, Rundetaarn for the cheap climb. Studenterhuset in the evening for hygge on a student budget.
Helsingør and Kronborg Castle (~45 min), then the Louisiana Museum at Humlebæk on the same line. Both mostly indoors, which is the point in late November.
Christiania, Assistens Cemetery and Jægersborggade. Harbour sauna and cold plunge at CopenHot (book). Tivoli Christmas in the evening, ~155-175 DKK, the one splurge worth it here.
Fly Copenhagen to Tallinn (~1h40). There is no rail link, so this flight is unavoidable. Afternoon: the Old Town and the Raekoja plats Christmas market, open since 20 Nov.
KGB Prison Cells at Pagari 1, the Kohtuotsa and Patkuli platforms for free rooftop panoramas, Balti Jaam Market. Kalma Saun in the evening: 1928 Art Deco bathhouse, wood-fired, the genuine local one.

Kalamaja on foot, the brutalist Linnahall and Patarei sea fortress on the waterfront, Telliskivi and Depoo. Heldeke! runs its mixed Sauna Social on Wednesdays, EUR 7.50 online. Põhjala Tap Room after.
Lux Express or Ecolines bus to Riga (~4h30). Eurail is no use on this corridor. Afternoon: Vecrīga on foot and the Doma laukums Christmas market, open since 27 Nov. Folkklubs Ala Pagrabs at night.
Riga Central Market in the five zeppelin hangars, then Alberta iela for the densest Art Nouveau facades in the world, and Miera iela. A proper pirts with the birch whisk in the evening.

Sigulda and the Gauja valley (~1h15 by train): Gutmanis Cave and Turaida Castle on the valley floor, since the cable car is closed for the season. Only 8h37 of daylight, so start at first light. Slow Riga day instead if it ices over.
Bus Riga to Vilnius (~4h); there is no direct train at all. Evening: the Cathedral Square tree and market, lit since 28 Nov, then Pilies Street.
Museum of Occupations and Freedom Fights in the former KGB HQ: the interrogation and execution cells. Then the Baroque Old Town and Užupis. Šnekutis for farmhouse ale and kepta duona.
Trakai island castle (~30 min by train) with kibinai by the lake, or Paneriai forest memorial plus Halės Turgus if you want the harder history. Alaus Biblioteka at night.

Lufthansa VNO to FRA, 2h15, earliest departure 06:25. BRANCH A: ICE to Dortmund (~2h10) for Borussia Dortmund vs Inter Milan, Champions League MD6, 21:00 at Signal Iduna Park, and sleep in Dortmund. BRANCH B: Römerberg Christmas market at dusk and an Apfelwein tavern in Sachsenhausen.
